text: Wait, they actually did it. GPT-4 is out. This changes everything about how I think about my job.
Just saw the announcement. Honestly not that surprised, we all knew it was coming. Let's see if it lives up to the hype.
I'm a radiologist. I just tested it on some case descriptions and I'm genuinely scared right now. It's frighteningly good.
Finally got access. The bar exam results alone are insane. 90th percentile. Let that sink in.
Another AI hype cycle. Remember when GPT-3 was going to change everything? I'll believe it when I see it deployed at scale.
My 8-year-old just asked it to help write a story. He was absolutely delighted. Whatever the implications for adults, kids are going to grow up with this as normal.
I've been in software for 20 years. I feel obsolete. Not exaggerating. I need to rethink my entire career.
The multimodal capabilities are wild. Feeding it an image of a handwritten equation and getting a worked solution back. Incredible.
People saying it'll replace programmers clearly haven't used it seriously. It's a great autocomplete, not a thinker. Calm down.
It failed basic spatial reasoning when I tested it. Still massive gaps. The hype is getting ahead of reality again.
I'm a teacher. My whole curriculum is now broken. Students can just generate essays instantly. I don't know what to do.
What a time to be alive. Genuinely excited and terrified in equal measure. History is happening in real time.
Used it to debug a nasty concurrency issue I've been stuck on for 3 days. Solved in 10 minutes. My productivity is going to go through the roof.
The safety team was clearly rushed. I found several jailbreaks in the first hour. OpenAI is moving too fast.
Tested it on my field (biochemistry). It's confident and mostly wrong on cutting-edge questions. Strong on textbook knowledge, weak on research frontiers.
The thing that gets me is it's going to keep improving. This is the worst it will ever be. That's a lot to process.
Everyone panicking about jobs — the economy has absorbed technological disruption before. We'll adapt. We always do.
I asked it to help me process my grief after losing my dad. It was surprisingly kind. I cried. I don't know what to make of that.
We're living through a genuine paradigm shift and half the internet is making memes. History won't be kind to how casually we greeted this.
Already seeing people use it to generate disinformation at scale. I work in fact-checking. The next election cycle is going to be a disaster.
The steerability improvements are impressive. You can actually shape its personality and communication style now. Much more useful for real workflows.
I just feel deeply uneasy. Can't explain it rationally. Something about the speed of this feels wrong.
Three hours in and I've already built a working prototype of an app I've been planning for months. The barrier to building has basically collapsed.
Honestly the most exciting day in tech since the iPhone launch. I remember where I was for that too. Same feeling.
My anxiety is through the roof. I have two kids to feed. If my job disappears I don't know what I do.
The coverage is so uncritical. No one is asking about the energy cost, the labour behind the training data, the IP implications. This is not just a cool product.
Used it to translate a letter from my grandmother who only speaks Cantonese. First time we've been able to communicate directly in 40 years. I'm overwhelmed.
The dust is settling. It's a powerful tool. Not magic, not the apocalypse. Just a very powerful tool we need to learn to use well.
Twelve hours of experiments done. My conclusion: transformative for some fields, marginal for others, and overhyped for most casual use cases. Nuance matters.
Whatever happens from here, something shifted today. I can feel it. My kids will ask me about this day in twenty years.
